answer_1.quote: We demonstrate symbolic knowledge distillation on the ATOMIC if-then resource. This follows an event-relation-inference (triple) format. The corpus links events (e.g. X attacks Y) to relations, e.g. HinderedBy which describes what might hinder an event. For a relation/event, the goal is to generate a resulting inference, e.g. X attacks Y HinderedBy X is restrained.
answer_1.outputs: The paper generates commonsense inferences in the form of event-relation-inference triples, such as 'X attacks Y HinderedBy X is restrained'.

answer_2.quote: We also estimate cross-entropy—how well a model trained on one corpus describes the other. From ATOMIC 10x to ATOMIC 2020, this is 9.31, only 2 points higher than its entropy suggesting ATOMIC 2020 is describable with information from ATOMIC 10x. In reverse, this is 41.48 suggesting much of ATOMIC 10x is not captured by ATOMIC 2020—ATOMIC 10x is surprising given only information from ATOMIC 2020.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluation with Amazon Mechanical Turk. 3 annotators rate each triple resulting in "accepted", "rejected" or "no judgement".
answer_4.guideline: Workers are presented with ATOMIC-style triples, replacing relations with natural language templates (e.g. HinderedBy becomes "can be hindered by"). 3 annotators rate each triple, with options for acceptability: "always/often", "sometimes/likely", "farfetched/never", "invalid", or "too unfamiliar to judge". The first two are considered "accepted", the second two "rejected" and the final is "no judgement".
